agent_testimony: Adjudicated the round against round.json, report.json, the six primary lane result files, and the isolated fixture diffs where patch-task comparability mattered. Key verdict: this round is useful internal evidence but not a clean comparative benchmark. Repo architecture audit, flow explanation, and bounded refactor plan stayed meaningfully anchored across lanes. Feature location, bug triage, safe change plan, small feature patch, seeded bug fix, code review diff, and docs drift were underanchored enough that the self-scores are visibly inflated relative to shared-task comparability. Round-level limitations that apply to every task: the parent accidentally injected a timebox interruption mid-run and later corrected it; m1nd-3 used a 0-5 scale and the parent mechanically clamped 31 score fields above 4 down to 4 with parent_normalization; seeded_bug_fix had no deterministic seeded failing test/bug artifact; code_review_diff had no supplied independent diff. Treat arm deltas as exploratory only, not public-claim material.

tests_or_commands_run: jq task summaries over the six primary lane result JSON files

task_results.notes: This was one of the cleanest benchmark tasks. All six primary lanes converged on the same architectural center of gravity around the public export layer, decorators, core runtime, and parser, so task-level arm comparison is usable here. The self-scores still run hot because most proof was static reading rather than independent runtime validation, but the underlying task was meaningfully shared.
evidence: All six lanes cited src/click/core.py, and five of six also cited the public facade/parser split.
The report marked comparable_primary_arms=true, and this task is one of the few where the semantic evidence supports that structural claim.
Lane totals still clustered at 22-24, which is slightly ceilinged given that proof was mostly file inspection rather than execution.

tests_or_commands_run: jq task summaries for bug_symptom_triage across the six primary lane result JSON files
sed -n on baseline Click docs/test/core snippets related to the nested-chain ambiguity
task_results.notes: The reasoning quality inside several lanes was good, but the benchmark task was too open-ended for comparison. The six lanes chose six different symptoms or symptom families: envvar batching, faulthandler stderr plumbing, callable-instance type naming, EchoingStdin.readlines, and two nested-chain variants. That makes the near-ceiling self-scores look inflated relative to what was actually shared.
evidence: All six lanes marked success, with totals from 22 to 24, even though they were not diagnosing one common symptom.
Two lanes converged on the nested-chain guard, while the other four targeted unrelated surfaces in core.py, testing.py, or types.py.
This task is informative about agent bug-hunting style, but weak as an arm-to-arm benchmark because the prompt supplied no common symptom fixture.
